sections.h2: Which Knox County offices deal with a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Five phone numbers cover nearly every Knox County tax question, and each leads to the Barbourville courthouse complex at 401 Court Square. The PVA's office sets the value. The sheriff bills and collects. The clerk inherits what goes unpaid, and the county attorney pursues it from there.

Knox County contacts, from the Kentucky Department for Local Government county listing
OfficeUse it forPhone
Property valuation administrator (PVA)Value, exemptions, appeal conferences(606) 546-4113
SheriffPaying the current bill(606) 546-3181
County clerkDeeds, delinquent certificates, filing an appeal(606) 546-3568
County attorneyDelinquent bills and payment talks(606) 546-9515
Fiscal courtGeneral county government(606) 546-6192

Courthouse doors open weekdays from 8:30 until 4:00. Saturday mornings until noon, only the county clerk and circuit clerk offices stay open. To record a deed on a Knox County house, carry it to the clerk on the first floor.

sections.h2: What is Knox County like for a homeowner thinking of selling?
sections.html:
Knox County spreads over 388 square miles at Kentucky's southeastern edge and shares borders with Clay, Bell, Whitley and Laurel counties. Barbourville, the seat, stands where Richland Creek joins the Cumberland River. U.S. 25E links it with Corbin, 16 miles to the northwest, and Pineville, the same distance southeast. Most of Corbin lies in Whitley County. Artemus and Flat Lick are the other named communities.

Lincoln County gave up land to form Knox on December 19, 1799. The Wilderness Road crosses it, and Barbourville saw the first land battle of the Civil War in Kentucky on September 19, 1861. Dr. Thomas Walker State Park holds a replica of the first house built in Kentucky. The courthouse that stands today, finished in 1964, is the fifth one. Coal mining carried the economy for generations, and Knox kept more of its jobs and residents than most coalfield counties did. Today the largest employers are in health care, retail and schools. Groundwork has begun on a Keeneland racetrack at the north end of the county, according to the fiscal court, and the Appalachian Wildlife Center is taking shape to the south.

sections.h2: How does Knox County's housing market look in the Census data?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 30,193 people in Knox County, and the July 2025 estimate is 29,532. That is a fall of 2.2 percent. The county holds 14,090 housing units, and the 2020 count found about one in eight of them empty. Census survey results covering 2020 through 2024 show a market with low prices and thin incomes:

  • Owners value a typical home they live in at $118,700.
  • Roughly two in three of the 11,711 households own their homes.
  • A typical monthly rent is $681.
  • A typical household takes in $32,527 a year, and 30.7 percent of residents live below the poverty line.
  • Three in four adults 25 and older finished high school.
  • Workers travel 24.4 minutes to their jobs on average.
  • The Bureau recorded no building permits for 2025.

When prices sit this low, a few thousand dollars of back tax takes a large bite out of a sale, so ask for payoff numbers before you list. Barbourville itself had 3,222 residents in 2020 and an estimated 3,081 in 2024.

sections.h2: Which school district covers a Knox County address?
sections.html:
Knox has three public school systems. Knox County Public Schools reaches every corner of the county. Barbourville Independent runs a single preschool-through-12 campus for the city. Corbin Independent serves Corbin, a district whose lines cross into two other counties. The county system operates schools named Central, Girdler, Flat Lick, Dewitt, Lynn Camp and Jesse D. Lay, among others.

A buyer comparing two houses a few blocks apart can find them in different systems. Give the parcel number to the PVA or the sheriff and ask which district applies before you quote a price or compare bills.

sections.h2: How does Knox County weather matter to a house?
sections.html:
NOAA's 1991 to 2020 normals for Barbourville show about 54 inches of rain and melted snow in an average year, falling on roughly 143 days. January lows average 24.6 degrees Fahrenheit and July highs reach 87. The record low is 22 below zero.

Steady moisture and hard freezes put roofs, gutters, crawlspaces and exposed plumbing at the top of an inspector's list. Sellers who keep receipts for recent repairs, or who tell a cash buyer plainly what needs work, shorten the back-and-forth. The same file supports an assessment conference if the PVA's value assumes a house in better shape than yours.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Knox County assessment?
sections.html:
Book a conference with the PVA first, since no appeal can be filed without one. After the May inspection window closes, the county clerk takes the appeal within a day, and a local board of fellow owners hears it a few weeks later.

Bring proof: photos, contractor bids, an appraisal or nearby sales. A board given nothing denies the appeal. The PVA's site says the office appraises everything at full market price, so recent nearby sales make the strongest argument.

sections.h2: When is the Knox County bill due, and what if it goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Property tax for the assessment year is due by December 31. The Department of Revenue notes that most sheriffs begin collecting in October or November. Discount and penalty steps differ across counties, so read the dates printed on your Knox County bill or call the sheriff at (606) 546-3181.

Anything still owed on April 15 goes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a lien on the parcel. The clerk's website offers a delinquent tax lookup and says the clerk's own figure controls at the time of sale. The state's worked example grows a $1,000 bill to $1,254 at transfer and to $1,659.90 after a June advertisement. Interest adds one percent per month, and the county attorney's 30-day and 60-day letters precede a sale to a third-party buyer. That buyer takes over the lien, and the owner then pays the buyer.

The person who owned the property on January 1 owes the bill personally, and under KRS 134.420 the lien lasts eleven years whoever holds the deed. A buyer inherits it with the house, so sellers clear it first.

sections.h2: Who gets the homestead exemption in Knox County?
sections.html: Anyone past their 65th birthday, and anyone ruled totally disabled by a retirement system, can deduct $49,100 from the assessed value for 2025 and 2026 if the house is their residence on January 1. File with the PVA by the end of December. Heirs living elsewhere do not inherit the break automatically.

sections.h2: How are taxes divided when a Knox County house sells?
sections.html:
The bill carries the January 1 owner's name, so a March sale still leaves the seller as taxpayer of record. The closing agent splits the year on the settlement statement and pays the sheriff. KRS 382.135(1)(d) requires an in-care-of address on the deed for that year's bill, so supply the buyer's mailing address.

Heirs, owners who fell behind and landlords with an empty rental often ask whether a cash buyer can wrap up everything in one closing. It works when the payoffs are known first: the sheriff quotes the current-year amount and the clerk quotes any older certificate. Ask the county attorney's office as well whether a payment plan is on file, since a title company will want that answer.

faqs.q: Which office collects Knox County property tax?
faqs.a: The sheriff, at (606) 546-3181, collects the current bill. After April 15 the clerk, at (606) 546-3568, handles it as a delinquent certificate.

faqs.q: How do I begin disputing a Knox County property value?
faqs.a: Schedule a conference with the PVA at (606) 546-4113. Filing with the clerk comes after that conference, before the deadline that follows the roll inspection.

faqs.q: How much does the Knox County homestead exemption remove?
faqs.a: It removes $49,100 of assessed value for 2025 and 2026 for qualifying seniors and totally disabled owners living in the house. Applications go to the PVA before the year ends.

faqs.q: Do late Knox County bills pick up interest?
faqs.a: Yes. After the bill reaches the clerk as a certificate, interest runs at one percent per month, with commissions and fees on top.

faqs.q: Could I sell a Knox County home that has unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays attached to the parcel, so the payoff is deducted at closing. Get written amounts from the sheriff and the clerk before you pick a date.
